evidence.accessibility: Preserves consumer-authored child semantics and does not introduce an interactive role.
evidence.state: Stateless; invalid ratios recover to the deterministic 1:1 default.
evidence.localization: Owns no visible copy or direction-sensitive behavior.
evidence.security: Accepts React children and runtime-strips the raw HTML escape hatch.
evidence.ssr: Native aspect-ratio styling produces deterministic server markup.
evidence.performance: Uses one wrapper and native CSS without measurement or observers.
evidence.ownership: Tale owns a CSS/native primitive rather than an upstream React Aria wrapper.
evidence.migration: Consumers can replace ad hoc aspect-ratio wrappers while retaining their child content.

evidence.accessibility: Uses native blockquote, paragraph, and footer semantics with consumer-authored attribution.
evidence.localization: All quoted content and attribution remain consumer-provided.
evidence.security: The cite attribute accepts credential-free absolute HTTP(S) URLs only and raw HTML is excluded.
evidence.performance: Adds no parser, observer, timer, or client-side state.
evidence.ownership: Tale owns the semantic composition; editor-only blockquote styling remains separate.
evidence.migration: Existing semantic blockquote markup maps directly to the Root, Content, and Attribution parts.

evidence.accessibility: Requires an accessible group or region name and fails invalid naming combinations closed to presentation.
evidence.state: Preserves React Aria Group interaction state without introducing selection semantics.
evidence.localization: Accessible names remain consumer-provided and logical orientation styling supports direction changes.
evidence.security: Excludes render-function content and the raw HTML escape hatch.
evidence.ssr: Role, orientation, and attached styling are deterministic across server and client.
evidence.performance: Wraps the pinned React Aria Group without measurement or additional subscriptions.
evidence.ownership: Tale restricts Group and owns naming, orientation, and attached styling.
evidence.migration: Action groups can migrate without adopting ToggleButtonGroup selection or SocialButtonGroup provider semantics.

records.rationale: Trust and document identity are outside the current catalog.

evidence.accessibility: Owns stable reference targets, ordinal labels, unavailable-source labels, and semantic ordered lists.
evidence.state: Normalizes one immutable document-local registry atomically and shares ordinals across repeated references.
evidence.localization: Source metadata is consumer content; UTC machine timestamps remain distinct from visible authored values.
evidence.security: Rejects malformed, credential-bearing, unsupported, and unbased relative URLs while escaping metadata.
evidence.ssr: Source order deterministically produces ordinals and document-local IDs.
evidence.performance: Builds one indexed normalized registry and reuses ordinal lookups.
evidence.ownership: Tale owns document identity, normalization, numbering, and URL policy.
evidence.migration: Link-based citations can move to explicit sources, references, and one source list without renumbering by hand.

evidence.accessibility: Uses the native inline code element and preserves text content.
evidence.localization: Treats code as opaque consumer text.
evidence.security: Escapes string children and never parses, highlights, fetches, or executes them.
evidence.performance: One inline element with no parser or highlighter.
evidence.ownership: Tale owns the inline semantic primitive while CodeBlock remains block-oriented.
evidence.migration: Existing inline code elements can adopt the component without changing their string data.

records.rationale: Overlay, focus, and selection state are outside the current catalog.

evidence.accessibility: Reuses Dialog focus containment and dismissal while owning item labels, control names, and focus restoration.
evidence.state: Provides mount-stable open and selection domains with atomic collection validation and fail-closed recovery.
evidence.localization: Default control names come from Tale localization and navigation follows the popup document direction.
evidence.security: Renders caller-owned React content without fetching media or exposing owned action handlers.
evidence.ssr: The first hydration remains closed or follows explicit deterministic state without browser-global identity.
evidence.performance: Indexes keys once per collection generation and limits swipe and focus work to the active instance.
evidence.ownership: Tale composes Dialog, Button, and swipe utilities into an item-keyed lightbox model.
evidence.migration: Existing modal galleries can retain their item data and move triggers, content, navigation, and captions incrementally.

records.rationale: Untrusted parsing is outside the current catalog.

evidence.accessibility: Maps the bounded document subset to semantic Tale and native elements without changing Chat announcements.
evidence.state: Parsing is synchronous and atomic; any validation, parser, or filtering failure renders only the fallback.
evidence.localization: Document text is consumer content and the invalid fallback can be localized by the consumer.
evidence.security: Gate A must prove limits, raw-HTML omission, non-fetching resource fallbacks, and strict URL filtering before export.
evidence.ssr: The selected parser must produce deterministic filtered output in Node 18 and browsers.
evidence.performance: Hard source, line, depth, and node limits bound work; the exact adversarial vector is benchmarked.
evidence.ownership: Tale owns the bounded renderer and adapter; Chat remains plain React content and text.
evidence.migration: Consumers opt into standalone Markdown explicitly without changing Chat runtime behavior or public API.

records.rationale: Document identity and observers are outside the current catalog.

evidence.accessibility: Renders a named navigation landmark with nested list and anchor semantics.
evidence.state: Owns mount-stable active state, per-instance observer generations, stale-work rejection, and deterministic reconciliation.
evidence.localization: Labels and landmark names remain consumer-provided; logical document order is preserved.
evidence.security: Resolves fragment targets only through the owning navigation document and does not accept arbitrary URLs.
evidence.ssr: The item tree and initial active marker are deterministic; observation begins only on the client.
evidence.performance: Uses one observer and at most one pending frame per instance.
evidence.ownership: Tale owns document navigation identity and observer behavior rather than extending Link alone.
evidence.migration: Existing in-page navigation can provide stable logical and target IDs while retaining authored labels.

records.rationale: Layout measurement and focus routing are outside the current catalog.

evidence.accessibility: Preserves item semantics and hands focus to the control, nearest visible item, or root before hiding focused content.
evidence.state: Owns deterministic measured partitions, convergence guards, generation cancellation, and ordered visibility callbacks.
evidence.localization: Item and overflow content remain consumer-rendered; start/end collapse uses logical ordering.
evidence.security: Accepts React render callbacks but no raw HTML or remote-resource capability.
evidence.ssr: Server and first hydration render all items before client-only measurement.
evidence.performance: Bounds settling passes, permits one partition update per frame, and measures fixed box vectors.
evidence.ownership: Tale owns the layout measurement and focus state machine.
evidence.migration: Existing action or breadcrumb rows can keep their item model and supply keyed item and overflow renderers.

records.rationale: Gesture and state callbacks are outside the current catalog.

evidence.accessibility: Owns separator naming, value ARIA, keyboard resizing, disabled/read-only behavior, and touch-capable movement.
evidence.state: Validates panel/handle topology and mount-stable size state with deterministic projection, acknowledgement, and cancellation.
evidence.localization: Horizontal movement follows writing direction while labels and value text remain consumer-configurable.
evidence.security: Runtime-strips owned action handlers and accepts no HTML or executable data.
evidence.ssr: Validated sizes produce deterministic flex bases; gestures and measurement begin only on the client.
evidence.performance: Uses direct react-aria useMove with bounded precision and no table-resize substitution.
evidence.ownership: Tale owns general panel topology, state, keyboard behavior, ARIA, and cancellation.
evidence.migration: General panels adopt the namespace directly; table-only ResizableTableContainer remains unrelated.

evidence.accessibility: Is always decorative and hidden from assistive technology; consumers own loading announcements.
evidence.state: Stateless apart from validated visual props.
evidence.localization: Owns no visible or assistive copy.
evidence.security: Renders an empty span and excludes children, raw HTML, roles, focus, and editable content.
evidence.ssr: Variant, dimensions, and animation classes render deterministically.
evidence.performance: One empty element with reduced-motion-aware CSS and no JavaScript animation loop.
evidence.ownership: Tale owns the decorative primitive; React Spectrum Skeleton is not a React Aria Components equivalent.
evidence.migration: Ad hoc decorative placeholders can move to explicit variants while retaining consumer-owned status text.

records.rationale: Locale, timezone, and clock ownership are outside the current catalog.

evidence.accessibility: Uses native time semantics with normalized machine-readable dateTime and visible localized output.
evidence.state: Owns immutable date normalization and a shared interval scheduler anchored to the supplied hydration clock.
evidence.localization: Requires explicit locale and timezone, freezes absolute presets, and uses Intl.RelativeTimeFormat for relative output.
evidence.security: Accepts only Date copies, finite epoch milliseconds, or complete offset-bearing timestamp strings.
evidence.ssr: Supplied now controls server and first hydration output before elapsed client time is applied.
evidence.performance: Groups relative subscribers by interval through Tale timer utilities and benchmarks 1,000 shared ticks.
evidence.ownership: Tale owns formatting, validation, hydration anchoring, and scheduling; applications choose locale, timezone, and now.
evidence.migration: Native time elements and app formatters can move to explicit absolute or relative Timestamp contracts.

records.rationale: Queues, timers, announcements, and leases are outside the current catalog.

evidence.accessibility: Owns polite/assertive announcements, localized region and dismiss labels, focus-safe dismissal, and one rendering lease.
evidence.state: Uses a stable Tale queue facade, replaceable raw generations, atomic publication, timers, pause reasons, and deterministic recovery.
evidence.localization: Region and dismiss defaults come from Tale localization; explicit valid labels override them.
evidence.security: Validates all queue/message inputs before mutation and exposes no unstable upstream record or queue type.
evidence.ssr: Region output is empty on the server and first hydration; lease ownership begins after mount.
evidence.performance: Bounds visible records, times only visible entries, and benchmarks the frozen 100-operation vector.
evidence.ownership: Tale isolates pinned unstable React Aria Toast primitives behind a stable public queue and Region API.
evidence.migration: Applications adopt the Tale queue factory and Region without depending on raw React Stately keys or timers.
